definitions.note: Usually used as a present subjunctive form (also used for commands with você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acenda a luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.note: Often used for turning on lights or lighting a fire/cigarette.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acender a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to turn on the living room light.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "acender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acendeu a luz da sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turned on the living room light.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "acender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acendi a luz do corredor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the hallway light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acenou para mim do outro lado da rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waved to me from the other side of the street.

definitions.note: Also used for the written accent mark on a letter in Portuguese (e.g., ´, ˆ, ~).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a strong accent.

definitions.note: Often used in the fixed phrase “acerca de” (about).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked about work yesterday.

definitions.native: to get right, to hit (a target)
definitions.note: Often used for getting something correct (an answer) or hitting a target.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He managed to get the answer right.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like "acertar detalhes" or "acertar uma data" (to settle/agree on details or a date).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s settle the details tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form meaning “I (did)”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got the answer right on the test.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/you formal/it) of "acertar"; often used for answers, guesses, or aiming at a target.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você acertou a resposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got the answer right.

definitions.note: Feminine form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle stayed lit all night.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As luzes estão acesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem acesso à internet aqui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have access to the internet here?

definitions.note: Common on signs/labels, especially in phrases like “acesso principal” (main entrance).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main entrance is on the left side of the building.

definitions.note: Very commonly used to mean “think/believe” (an opinion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acha que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thinks it’s going to rain today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acha as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds the keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural of "achar" (they/you plural think; they/you plural find).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acham que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: From the verb "achar"; often used to express an opinion ("to think").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achamos que este restaurante é muito bom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think this restaurant is very good.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "achar"; often used to mean "thinking" (opinion) or "finding" (discovering/locating), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou achando que ele vai se atrasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he’s going to be late.

definitions.note: Often means “to think” in everyday speech (“I think…”). It can also mean “to find” in the sense of locating something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acho que ele está em casa, mas não tenho certeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he is at home, but I'm not sure.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "achar" used with "eles/elas/vocês".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acharam as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the keys on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acharia isso estranho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would find that strange.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) present tense of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu achas que vai chover hoje?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you think it’s going to rain today?

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "achar" used with "tu" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achaste as chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "achar" (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or background description).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought he was going to arrive earlier.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they). Often means “thought” in everyday speech; can also mean “found” (discovered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles achavam que o filme ia ser chato, mas gostaram muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the movie was going to be boring, but they liked it a lot.

definitions.note: From the verb “achar”; it can mean “to think” (opinion) or “to find” (discover/locate), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acho que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used to express an opinion or guess ("I thought / I figured"). Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of "achar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achei que você ia chegar mais cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you were going to arrive earlier.

definitions.note: often used to give your opinion (usually followed by “que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acho que vai chover hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: in the sense of locating something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não acho meu celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t find my phone.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você) of “achar”. In many contexts it can also mean “thought” (as in giving an opinion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela achou as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found the keys on the couch.

definitions.native: thought, found (in the sense of an opinion)
definitions.note: Used to express what someone thought/considered (ele/ela/você in the simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu perguntei, e ele achou a ideia boa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked, and he thought the idea was good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, eu te liguei acidentalmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I called you accidentally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve um acidente na estrada esta manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was an accident on the road this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve muitos acidentes na estrada por causa da chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many accidents on the road because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O quadro está acima da cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The painting is above the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acompanha a irmã até a escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanies her sister to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acompanha as notícias todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He follows the news every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chegou acompanhado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He arrived accompanied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O frango vem com acompanhamento de arroz e salada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chicken comes with a side dish of rice and salad.

definitions.note: Often used for ongoing support or checking progress (e.g., medical or project follow-up).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has medical follow-ups every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acompanhar você até a estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to accompany you to the station.

definitions.native: to follow, to keep up with
definitions.note: Often used for following news, a series, instructions, or someone’s progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acompanho as notícias todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I follow the news every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "acompanhar"; often used after expressions like "se" (if) or "como se" (as if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ela me acompanhasse, eu me sentiria mais seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If she accompanied me, I would feel safer.

definitions.note: Often used as a command or suggestion (e.g., “Follow me/us”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acompanhe o guia até a saída.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the guide to the exit.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite invitation or request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acompanhe-me até a recepção.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come with me to the reception desk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acompanhou o amigo até a estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanied her friend to the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acompanhou as notícias durante a semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept track of the news during the week.

definitions.note: Informal (especially Brazilian Portuguese) spelling/pronunciation of "acompanhar" (dropping the final -r in the infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou acompanhá até a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll walk you to the door.

definitions.note: Often used for places or atmospheres (e.g., a room, a home, a café).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este apartamento é muito aconchegante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment is very cozy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela aconselha o aluno a estudar todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advises the student to study every day.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (often used as a past participle, e.g., with 'ser'/'estar')
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi aconselhada a descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was advised to rest.

definitions.note: Often used in impersonal/passive constructions like “é aconselhado...” (“it is advised/recommended...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não é aconselhado nadar aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is not advised to swim here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aconselhei o meu amigo a descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advised my friend to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu aconselho você a descansar um pouco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advise you to rest a bit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me aconselhou a descansar mais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advised me to rest more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso acontece todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That happens every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Coisas estranhas acontecem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Strange things happen at night.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “acontecer”; often used with “estar” to mean “to be happening.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que está acontecendo aqui?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is happening here?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O que vai acontecer amanhã?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is going to happen tomorrow?

definitions.note: Literary/formal; this is the simple pluperfect (mais-que-perfeito simples). In everyday speech, Portuguese usually uses “tinha acontecido”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu cheguei, isso já acontecera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, that had already happened.

definitions.note: Can also be the future subjunctive form, often used after words like “se” (if) or “quando” (when): “se/quando isso acontecera” ≈ “if/when that happens”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se isso acontecera, ligue para mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If that happens, call me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muitas coisas aconteceram ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many things happened last night.

definitions.note: Conditional form (often used for hypotheticals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu achei que isso aconteceria ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought that would happen yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O evento acontecerá amanhã à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The event will happen tomorrow night.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive (imperfect subjunctive) of “acontecer”; often used after expressions like “se” (if) or to talk about a hypothetical past situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se isso acontecesse, eu ficaria muito preocupado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If that happened, I would be very worried.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente aconteceu ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happened yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nada disso tinha acontecido antes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: None of that had happened before.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve muitos acontecimentos importantes este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many important events this year.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "acontecer" (used after expressions of doubt, desire, possibility, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que isso não aconteça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that doesn't happen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sempre acorda cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always wakes up early.

definitions.note: Informal command (tu).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up! It’s already late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela já está acordada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is already awake.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças estão acordadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are awake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acordado desde as seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like estar/ficar (e.g., estar acordado = to be awake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou acordado desde as seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Used when something has been agreed on (often in contexts like “como foi acordado” = “as agreed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O preço foi acordado ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price was agreed on yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; used for a group of men or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças ainda estão acordadas, mas os pais já estão acordados também.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are still awake, but the parents are awake too.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordam cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wake up early every day.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition, e.g. "acordar com" (agree with) or "acordar em" (agree on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordam com a proposta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They agree with the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso acordar cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “com” (to agree with someone) or “em” (to agree on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós acordamos em um preço justo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on a fair price.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acordaram cedo para pegar o ônibus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They woke up early to catch the bus.

definitions.native: used to wake up, was waking up
definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acordava cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to wake up early every day.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acorde cedo amanhã, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up early tomorrow, please.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) in the simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordei cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acordo cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up early every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement on the price.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular of “acordar” (he/she/it woke up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele acordou cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He woke up early today.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech/writing as a shortened form of “acordar” (especially in some Brazilian Portuguese varieties).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso acordá cedo amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early during the week.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive or noun (e.g., "acostumado a acordar cedo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou acostumado a acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to waking up early.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are already used to the cold.

definitions.native: getting used to, getting accustomed to

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso me acostumar a acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get used to waking up early.

definitions.native: I got used to, I became accustomed to

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got used to the weather here.

definitions.native: got used to, became accustomed to

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got used to the new job quickly.

definitions.note: Usually used with ele/ela/você (present tense).

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) present tense of "acreditar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed the story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela acreditará na sua história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will believe your story.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will think that he arrives early.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (tu) form; common in Portugal and in informal contexts where "tu" is used.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you really believe that?

definitions.note: Imperfect past; can describe an ongoing belief in the past or a habitual belief (“used to believe”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu acreditava que ele ia chegar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed he was going to arrive early.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you-pl believed; also used for ongoing/habitual past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles acreditavam que tudo ia dar certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed that everything would work out.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (“Believe me!”) or as a polite form in phrases like “acredite em mim”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acredite em mim, vai dar tudo certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, everything will work out.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acreditei na sua história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed your story.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu). Often used to express an opinion or belief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acredito que ele está certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe (that) he is right.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believed his story.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “andar” for ele/ela/você.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ganhou um anel de prata no aniversário.

definitions.note: Person who receives guests (at home, an event, or on a TV/radio show).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles me chamam todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They call me every day.

definitions.note: Present tense (nós). Can also mean “we name” or “we invite” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chamamos o médico agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We call the doctor now.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “chamar” (used with “estar” or to mean “while/by calling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chamando o médico agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calling the doctor now.

definitions.note: Often used for calling someone on the phone, calling out to someone, or calling someone/something by a name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou chamar a minha mãe mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call my mom later.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chamar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chamaram um táxi depois do show.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called a taxi after the show.

definitions.note: Often used after conjunctions like "quando" (when) or "se" (if), meaning something like “when/if they call…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chamarem você, pode entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they call you, you can come in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chamas estavam muito altas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flames were very high.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação habitual/contínua no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu era criança, eu chamava a minha avó todos os domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I called my grandma every Sunday.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all called; they/you all were calling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chamavam o professor de "doutor".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called the professor "doctor".

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used as an affirmative formal command: “call!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você me chame amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you call me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu te chamei ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you last night.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês / eles / elas) form of "chamar"; also used for affirmative commands to "vocês" (e.g., "Chamem o médico!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que chamem o médico a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they call the doctor in time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saiu fumaça pela chaminé da casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoke came out through the house’s chimney.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu). Often used to say your name: “Eu me chamo …” = “My name is …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chamo o garçom quando preciso de ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call the waiter when I need help.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chamar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me chamou ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She called me last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos brindar com champanhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s toast with champagne.

definitions.note: Colloquial spoken form of "chamar" (often used in Brazil), typically before a pronoun: "chamá ele" = "chamar ele".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou chamá você mais tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call you later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu tive a chance de falar com ela ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the chance to talk to her yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem boas chances de passar no exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a good chance of passing the exam.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "chantagear" (used like “blackmailing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está me chantageando para eu fazer o que ele quer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is blackmailing me so that I do what he wants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou chantagear o colega para conseguir dinheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to blackmail his coworker to get money.

definitions.note: Informal/slang, usually about being under the influence of drugs (sometimes alcohol).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está chapado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is high.

definitions.note: Often used for something very flat or pressed flat (e.g., metal, a tire, a surface).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pneu está chapado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire is flat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou um chapéu novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a new hat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os chapéus estão na prateleira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hats are on the shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muito charme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of charm.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "chato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aquele barulho é muito chata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is very annoying.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "chato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A palestra ficou chata depois de um tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lecture got boring after a while.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou chateada com o comentário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got upset about the comment.

definitions.note: Often used to describe feeling upset or bothered (can mean “bummed” in casual contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chateado com o que aconteceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m upset about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi muito chato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very boring.

definitions.note: Plural form; used to describe people/things (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses filmes são muito chatos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those movies are very boring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdi a chave de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the house key.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, "chave" is also commonly used in tool names, like "chave de fenda" (screwdriver) and "chave inglesa" (adjustable wrench).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem uma chave para apertar esse parafuso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a wrench to tighten this screw?

definitions.note: Plural of "chave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Onde estão as chaves do carro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are the car keys?

definitions.note: Also commonly means “we check (something) out” in Brazilian Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Checamos os documentos antes de assinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We check the documents before signing.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese; in some contexts you can also use "verificar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou checar o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check the email before leaving.

definitions.note: Loanword from English; in Portuguese this is often written as “cheque”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um check.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Nationality/demonym; can also be used as an adjective (“Czech”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O checo mora em Praga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Czech man lives in Prague.

definitions.note: Informal; from the verb “checar” (common in Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele checou o e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He checked the email before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu chefe chega cedo todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss arrives early every day.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "chegar"; can also be used for "you arrive/come" with "você".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus chega às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus arrives at eight.

definitions.note: Common as an interjection meaning “that’s enough/stop.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chega, eu já entendi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough, I already understood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chegada do ônibus foi atrasada por causa do trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus’s arrival was delayed because of traffic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tinha chegado cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had arrived early.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in the expression “amigos chegados” (“close friends”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são amigos chegados desde a escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been close friends since school.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "chegar" (they arrive / you all arrive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegam às oito todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrive at eight every day.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "chegar" with "we" (nós).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegamos ao aeroporto bem cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived at the airport very early.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "chegar"; often used after "estar" to mean "is/are arriving" or "is/are coming".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou chegando em casa agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m arriving home now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chego em casa às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get home at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles chegaram cedo ao aeroporto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They arrived early at the airport.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive of "chegar" used after certain conjunctions/prepositions; typically means "(for them) to arrive" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos esperar eles chegarem antes de começar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to wait for them to arrive before starting.

definitions.native: we will arrive, we will get there
definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaremos ao aeroporto às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will arrive at the airport at eight.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "chegar" (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegaria mais cedo se não houvesse trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would arrive earlier if there weren’t traffic.

definitions.note: Often used after time/condition words like "quando" (when) or "se" (if), referring to a future situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando chegarmos, eu te ligo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrive, I'll call you.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive; often used after prepositions like "para" (in order to) or "até" (until).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos sair cedo para chegarmos a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's leave early so we can arrive on time.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O trem chegará às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will arrive at eight.

definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você). Often used with "a" (e.g., chegar a algum lugar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chegará ao aeroporto cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will get to the airport early.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "chegar"; used after expressions like "if" or "I wanted that" to talk about a hypothetical/desired past situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se ele chegasse mais cedo, nós sairíamos juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he arrived earlier, we would go out together.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; common in European Portuguese and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chegaste tarde ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You arrived late yesterday.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chegava em casa por volta das seis todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived home around six every day.

definitions.native: I arrive, I get (to), I reach
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chego em casa às seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get home at six.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it arrived; you arrived; also used for “you” in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chegou em casa tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He arrived home late.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "chegar" (also used for formal commands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você chegue cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you arrive early.

definitions.note: First-person singular in the past (pretérito perfeito) of "chegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheguei em casa às oito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got home at eight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (vocês/eles/elas) and also the affirmative command for vocês.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cheguem a tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they arrive on time.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A garrafa está cheia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is full.

definitions.note: Used especially in the expression “cheia do rio” (river flood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cheia do rio alagou a cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flood flooded the city.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “cheio”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As garrafas estão cheias de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottles are full of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O copo está cheio de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is full of water.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of "cheio" (used with masculine plural nouns, or mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os copos estão cheios de água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cups are full of water.

definitions.note: Usually used with "a" + noun: "cheira a" = "smells like".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo cheira a mofo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells like mold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cachorro está cheirando o chão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sniffing the ground.

definitions.note: Can mean either to sense an odor (with your nose) or to have a smell (give off an odor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este queijo está a cheirar mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cheese smells bad.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A cozinha cheirava a pão fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen smelled like fresh bread.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "cheirar" (also used in some formal commands, e.g., "Cheire isto.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu cheire melhor amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I smell better tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que cheiro bom de café!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a nice smell of coffee!

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (for você), meaning “check/verify.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cheque as informações antes de confirmar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the information before confirming.

definitions.note: In Brazilian Portuguese, people often write "cheque" as "cheque"; in English, "cheque" is the British spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele pagou com um cheque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paid with a check.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), 1st-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chequei meu e-mail antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked my email before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem um chiclete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any chewing gum?

definitions.note: Often refers to casual open footwear (like flip-flops).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não esqueça de levar os chinelos para a piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to bring your flip-flops to the pool.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é chinesa e mora no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Chinese and lives in Brazil.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (used for women or feminine plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As estudantes chinesas falam português muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese students speak Portuguese very well.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of the adjective (also used for mixed-gender groups)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os restaurantes chineses desta rua são muito bons.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese restaurants on this street are very good.

definitions.note: Plural of "chinês"; can refer to a group of Chinese people (often men/mixed group depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos chineses morando aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Chinese people living here.

definitions.note: Can describe something from China or the Chinese language; as an adjective it agrees in gender/number with the noun it modifies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Chinese at school.

definitions.note: Can refer to a Chinese person or, in some contexts, the Chinese language; here it’s used as a noun for a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chinês mora aqui há dois anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Chinese man has lived here for two years.

definitions.note: As a noun, it can also mean the Chinese language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estou aprendendo chinês na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Chinese at school.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou chocada com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was shocked by the news.

definitions.note: Often used for people reacting to surprising or upsetting news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei chocado com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was shocked by the news.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles ficaram chocados com a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were shocked by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia foi chocante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was shocking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto de chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei chocolates para a festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought chocolates for the party.

definitions.note: Often used with the sense of emotionally shocking/offending someone; can also mean causing a collision (crashed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A notícia chocou muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news shocked a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente causou um choque entre dois carros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident caused a collision between two cars.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “chorar” (to cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela chora quando vê filmes tristes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cries when she watches sad movies.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças choram quando estão cansadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children cry when they are tired.

definitions.note: Can be present indicative (“we cry”) or simple past/preterite (“we cried”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem, choramos no fim do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, we cried at the end of the movie.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "chorar"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está chorando porque perdeu o celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is crying because she lost her phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela começou a chorar quando ouviu a notícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She started to cry when she heard the news.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ação habitual ou contínua no passado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eu era criança, eu chorava quando perdia meu brinquedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to cry when I lost my toy.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "chorar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu chorei quando vi o filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cried when I watched the movie.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu): “I cry” / “I weep”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Às vezes eu choro quando vejo um filme triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I cry when I watch a sad movie.

definitions.note: Simple past (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chorou no final do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cried at the end of the movie.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "chover"; used after expressions of doubt, desire, or conditions (e.g., "Espero que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que chova amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it rains tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular present of "chover"; in Portuguese this verb is usually used impersonally (no real subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje chove o dia todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rains all day today.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "chover"; commonly used with "estar" (e.g., "está chovendo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está chovendo muito hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje vai chover à tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's going to rain this afternoon.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of "chover".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã choverá à tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will rain in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) of "chover"; often used impersonally (without a subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem choveu muito na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it rained a lot in the city.

definitions.note: Imperfect past of "chover"; often used for ongoing or habitual past weather.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando saí de casa, chovia muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I left home, it was raining a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem chovido muito esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has rained a lot this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cano antigo é feito de chumbo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old pipe is made of lead.

definitions.note: Especially common in Brazil; can refer both to the grilled meat and to the social event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No domingo, fizemos um churrasco com a família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday, we had a barbecue with the family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chute a bola!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kick the ball!

definitions.note: Informal: often used to mean “guess” (as in making a quick guess).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Chute um número de 1 a 10.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess a number from 1 to 10.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deu um chute na bola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kicked the ball.

definitions.note: Common in the expression “dar um chute” (to take a guess).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dá um chute: quantas pessoas vêm à festa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a guess: how many people are coming to the party?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele chutou a bola para o gol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kicked the ball toward the goal.

definitions.note: Common in Brazilian Portuguese: “chutar” can mean to guess (often without being sure).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não sei a resposta; eu só chutei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know the answer; I just guessed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A chuva começou de repente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain started suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chuvas fortes causaram alagamentos na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heavy rains caused flooding in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chuveiro do hotel não estava funcionando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel shower wasn’t working.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje está um dia chuvoso.
