definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lying down on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone/something in a horizontal position (e.g., on a bed or on the ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está deitado no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is lying down on the couch.

definitions.native: to lie down, to lay down
definitions.note: Often used reflexively as “deitar-se” = “to lie down / go to bed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deitar mais cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to lie down earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (especially with “se”: “deite-se” = “lie down”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deite-se, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lie down, please.

definitions.native: I lay down, I put down
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito) of "deitar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou cansado, então deitei no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm tired, so I lay down on the couch.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular of “deitar” (he/she/it/you-formal lay down / put down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deitou no sofá e dormiu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lay down on the couch and fell asleep.

definitions.note: Usually means “lets/allows” (3rd person singular, present). It can also be used as an informal command meaning “leave it / stop it,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela não deixa eu sair à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She doesn't let me go out at night.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "deixar"; often used with "ser/estar" to form the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bolsa foi deixada no ônibus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bag was left on the bus.

definitions.note: Feminine plural past participle of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves foram deixadas na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were left on the table.

definitions.note: Past participle of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro foi deixado na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was left on the table.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vós) command form; mostly seen in older, literary, or religious Portuguese.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixai as crianças brincarem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) form of “deixar”; it can mean to leave something/someone somewhere or to allow/let something happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixam as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: From deixar; it can mean physically leaving something/someone or allowing/letting something happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixamos as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “deixar”; often used like “leaving” or “letting” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou deixando as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to let/allow” (e.g., deixar alguém fazer algo = to let someone do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode deixar a mala aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave the suitcase here.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito), 3rd person plural: “they left.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram a cidade ontem à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the city last night.

definitions.note: Often used with an object meaning “left something somewhere” or “let/allowed.” Simple past, 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixaram as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “deixar” (often used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu deixaria as chaves na mesa, se você quiser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would leave the keys on the table, if you want.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixará as chaves na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) future tense of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles deixarão as malas no hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will leave the suitcases at the hotel.

definitions.note: Present tense (tu). Informal “you” in many regions; in Brazil it’s mostly used in some dialects and in Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu deixas a porta aberta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you leave the door open?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used after "se" (if) to express a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu deixasse a porta aberta, o gato fugia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I left the door open, the cat would run away.

definitions.native: you left, you let, you allowed
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito), informal singular (tu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixaste a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the door open.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (ongoing/habitual action in the past) of “deixar” (“to leave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deixava o carro na garagem todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the car in the garage every day.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands: “let/leave …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixe a porta aberta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave the door open.

definitions.native: I left, I let, I allowed
definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito), 1st person singular of “deixar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixei o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the book on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixem as crianças brincar no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the children play in the park.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deixem o carro aqui e venham comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the car here and come with me.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also the informal imperative) of “deixar” (used with “tu”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que não deixes a porta aberta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't leave the door open.

definitions.note: First-person singular ("I") present tense of "deixar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu deixo o livro na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the book on the table.

definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você) of “deixar”; can mean either leaving something somewhere or allowing something to happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deixou o celular em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She left her cell phone at home.

definitions.note: Colloquial shortened form of “deixar”, common in informal speech and lyrics (especially in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou deixá pra depois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll leave it for later.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "ela".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este livro é dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is hers.

definitions.note: Contraction of “de” + “ela”; used to show possession or relation (e.g., “the book is hers”, “a friend of hers”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O livro é dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is hers.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "elas"; refers to a group of females (or mixed group treated as feminine in context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A casa delas fica perto daqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their house is close to here.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "ele"; often used after a noun to show possession (like "his").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro dele é vermelho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His car is red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou à delegacia para registrar a ocorrência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the police station to file the report.

definitions.note: Used for a masculine or mixed group (or when the possessed noun is masculine). For an all-female group, use "delas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este carro é deles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car is theirs.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "eles" (masculine/mixed plural); contrasts with "delas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro deles está na garagem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their car is in the garage.

definitions.note: Informal; common in Brazilian Portuguese (from English “delete”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deletou a mensagem por engano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deleted the message by mistake.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está numa situação delicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in a delicate situation.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (often about a person’s manner or feelings)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A professora foi muito delicada com as crianças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher was very gentle with the children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tratou o assunto com delicadeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handled the matter with gentleness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi uma delicadeza da sua parte me ligar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was very kind/thoughtful of you to call me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este copo é muito delicado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This glass is very delicate.

definitions.note: Often used for people or topics/situations that require tact.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É um assunto delicado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive topic.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A sopa está deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is delicious.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As sobremesas estão deliciosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The desserts are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bolo está delicioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is delicious.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of “delicioso”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os pastéis estão deliciosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pastries are delicious.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone speaking incoherently (e.g., from fever, illness, exhaustion, or intense emotion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele estava delirando de febre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was delirious with fever.

definitions.note: Often used for speaking incoherently due to fever/illness, extreme emotion, or (sometimes) in a joking way meaning someone is talking nonsense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Com a febre alta, ele começou a delirar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the high fever, he started to be delirious.

definitions.note: Often used to say something (especially food) is really good: “Que delícia!” = “How delicious!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O bolo de chocolate estava uma delícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate cake was a real treat.

definitions.note: Used to express excess.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você trabalha demais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You work too much.

definitions.note: Often used (especially in speech) to intensify meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto demais deste livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this book a lot.

definitions.note: Usually used with an article (e.g., "os demais", "as demais") meaning "the others/the rest".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu falei com a Ana, e os demais chegaram depois.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with Ana, and the others arrived later.

definitions.note: Often used for demand in a market/economic sense (supply and demand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A demanda por energia aumentou este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Demand for energy increased this year.

definitions.note: Used in legal contexts to mean a lawsuit or claim filed in court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele entrou com uma demanda contra a empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He filed a lawsuit against the company.

definitions.note: Often placed after the adjective/adverb it modifies (e.g., "caro demais" = "too expensive").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este café está quente demais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This coffee is too hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está demasiado frio aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s too cold here.

definitions.note: Often used for being fired (dismissal) or having your employment terminated; contrast with "pedido de demissão" (resignation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa anunciou a demissão de cem funcionários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company announced the dismissal of one hundred employees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem demiti um funcionário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I fired an employee.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "demitir"; often used with "ser/estar" or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela foi demitida ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was fired yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "demitir"; often used with "ser/estar" to mean someone has been fired from a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi demitido ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fired yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for firing someone from a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa decidiu demitir vários funcionários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to fire several employees.

definitions.note: Used when someone leaves an official position voluntarily (e.g., a minister, director).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ministro decidiu demitir-se após o escândalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister decided to resign after the scandal.

definitions.note: Past tense (third person singular): “(he/she/it) fired/dismissed” or “(you, formal) fired/dismissed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa demitiu o funcionário ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired the employee yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A democracia depende de eleições livres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Democracy depends on free elections.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela defende uma sociedade mais democrática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advocates for a more democratic society.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela demonstrou interesse em aprender português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed interest in learning Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve uma demora de vinte minutos no atendimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a twenty-minute delay in the service.

definitions.note: From the verb "demorar"; often used to talk about how long something takes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quanto tempo demora para chegar lá?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How long does it take to get there?

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "demorar"; often used with "estar" to say something is taking a long time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus está demorando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is taking a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus vai demorar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is going to take a while.

definitions.native: will take (time), will take a while
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus demorará cerca de 20 minutos para chegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus will take about 20 minutes to arrive.

definitions.native: I took (a long time), I was late
definitions.note: Past tense (eu) of “demorar”; often used to say you took longer than expected to arrive or finish something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, demorei para chegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I took a long time to arrive.

definitions.native: took a long time, took (a while)
definitions.note: Past tense (ele/ela/você) of "demorar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ônibus demorou, mas chegou no fim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus took a while, but it arrived in the end.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nós) of "dar"; often used to make suggestions or invitations ("let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos embora, mas antes demos um presente à Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s leave, but first let’s give Ana a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dizem que a casa está cheia de demônios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say the house is full of demons.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A neblina estava densa de manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fog was dense in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela marcou uma consulta dental para amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She scheduled a dental appointment for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso ir ao dentista porque estou com dor de dente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to go to the dentist because I have a toothache.

definitions.note: Plural of "dente".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escovo os dentes depois do jantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brush my teeth after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou ao dentista amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the dentist tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a superlative or to highlight one item within a group (e.g., “the best among…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dentre todos os alunos, ela foi a que mais estudou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Among all the students, she was the one who studied the most.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "dentro de" = "inside/within (of)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gato está dentro de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is inside the house.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "dentro de" = "inside/within" (a place, container, time period, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gato está dentro de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is inside the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O departamento de vendas fica no terceiro andar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sales department is on the third floor.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Brazil to mean an apartment (housing unit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles alugaram um departamento no centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rented an apartment downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa tem vários departamentos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company has several departments.

definitions.note: Common in Brazil to refer to apartments (short for “apartamentos”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles alugaram dois departamentos perto da praia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rented two apartments near the beach.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “depende de” (“it depends on”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depende do dia e do horário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It depends on the day and the time.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present of "depender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles dependem dos pais para pagar a faculdade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They depend on their parents to pay for college.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós dependemos do ônibus para ir ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We depend on the bus to get to work.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (e.g., depender de alguém/algo = to depend on someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isso vai depender do que você decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That will depend on what you decide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela depilou as pernas ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waxed her legs yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("depois de") to mean "after" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois, eu vou ligar para você.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Afterwards, I’ll call you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fala depressa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak quickly, please.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a mood, symptoms, or a clinical condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele anda muito depressivo ultimamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s been very depressed lately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A depressão pode afetar o sono e o apetite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Depression can affect sleep and appetite.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O final do filme foi bem deprimente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ending of the movie was really depressing.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to describe a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está deprimida desde que perdeu o emprego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been depressed since she lost her job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da notícia, ele ficou deprimido por dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he was depressed for days.

definitions.note: Often used for a bank deposit or a security deposit (e.g., for renting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso fazer um depósito na minha conta hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to make a deposit into my account today.

definitions.note: Also used for a place where goods are stored.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O depósito da loja fica no fundo do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store’s warehouse is at the back of the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou der o livro para a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to give the book to Ana.

definitions.note: Simple pluperfect (mais-que-perfeito simples); common in writing and storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela já me dera o endereço antes de sair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had already given me the address before leaving.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "dar" for "they" (or "you" plural in Portugal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles me deram um presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me a present.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "derramar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, eu derramei o café na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I spilled the coffee on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele derramou café na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spilled coffee on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gelo derrete rápido no sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ice melts quickly in the sun.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "derreter"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gelo está derretendo no sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ice is melting in the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chocolate começou a derreter no sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate started to melt in the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O chocolate derreteu no sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate melted in the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A derrota no jogo foi difícil para o time.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defeat in the game was hard for the team.

definitions.note: Often used as the past participle of "derrotar"; it can also function as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O time foi derrotado na final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team was defeated in the final.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O nosso time conseguiu derrotar o adversário na final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team managed to defeat the opponent in the final.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O time derrotou o rival na final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team defeated the rival in the final.

definitions.native: they knocked down, they brought down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles derrubaram a parede para ampliar a sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They knocked down the wall to make the room bigger.

definitions.native: I knocked down, I brought down, I toppled
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Derrubei o copo sem querer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knocked the cup over without meaning to.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "derrubar" (he/she/it/you formal) or "you" (informal, Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O vento forte derrubou a árvore.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The strong wind knocked down the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A ponte desabou durante a tempestade.

definitions.note: Often used for turning off devices or engines; also used for ending a phone call.

definitions.note: Command form addressed to “you” (plural) or used as a formal command.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn off your cell phones during the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used for a small mistake or misstep (e.g., in speech, writing, or behavior).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was just a slip; it won’t happen again.

definitions.note: Often used for moving something/someone from one place/position to another.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved the chair closer to the window.

definitions.note: Used for a joint (like a shoulder, arm, finger) coming out of place.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dislocated his shoulder during the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A vista do miradouro é deslumbrante.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela desmaiou no meio da aula.

definitions.note: Often used for buildings/structures, but it can also be used figuratively for plans or hopes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A parede desmoronou depois da tempestade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall collapsed after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse comentário foi desnecessário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment was unnecessary.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses comentários são desnecessários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments are unnecessary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu preciso comprar desodorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy deodorant.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi desonesto comigo e mentiu sobre o que aconteceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was dishonest with me and lied about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My room is disorganized.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois de acordar, ele ficou desorientado por alguns minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After waking up, he was disoriented for a few minutes.

definitions.native: I fired, I dismissed, I let go
definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of “despedir” in the 1st person singular: “eu despedi” (used for ending someone’s employment).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fired the employee yesterday.

definitions.native: I said goodbye, I bid farewell
definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of “despedir” in the 1st person singular: “eu despedi” (used with “me”/“nos” for taking leave).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I said goodbye to my friends at the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A despedida foi emocionante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farewell was moving.

definitions.note: Past participle of “despedir”. Often used with “ser/estar” (e.g., “foi despedido”, “está despedido”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi despedido ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fired yesterday.

definitions.native: to say goodbye, to bid farewell
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fui ao aeroporto para me despedir dos meus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went to the airport to say goodbye to my friends.

definitions.native: to fire, to dismiss (from a job)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa decidiu despedir alguns funcionários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to fire some employees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele se despediu dos amigos na estação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said goodbye to his friends at the station.

definitions.note: Used when someone loses a job (more common than in English to use the same verb as “say goodbye”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A empresa o despediu sem aviso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired him without notice.

definitions.note: Past (he/she/you formal) form of "despejar"; often used for liquids ("poured out") or for getting rid of something ("threw out").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She poured the water into the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A despensa está cheia de arroz e feijão.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They waste a lot of food every day.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "desperdiçar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are wasting water by leaving the tap on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não quero desperdiçar comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to waste food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele desperdiçou muito dinheiro com coisas que não precisava.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wasted a lot of money on things he didn’t need.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting resources like time, money, food, or water.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O desperdício de comida é um problema sério.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Food waste is a serious problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu coloquei o despertador para as seis da manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set the alarm clock for six in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela despertou cedo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She woke up early today.

definitions.note: Plural of "despesa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As despesas do mês foram mais altas do que esperávamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This month's expenses were higher than we expected.

definitions.note: Common in European Portuguese; in Brazilian Portuguese, the usual word is "esporte".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto de praticar desporto ao ar livre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to play sports outdoors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está despreocupado com o que os outros vão pensar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is unconcerned about what others are going to think.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela despreza as regras do time.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She despises the team's rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela falou com desprezo sobre os colegas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spoke with contempt about her coworkers.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essa" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito dessa música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this song.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essa" (feminine singular of "esse/essa").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto dessa música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (de + essa). Used before feminine singular nouns; also used to refer back to something previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto dessa comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like this food.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essas" (feminine plural of "esse"); used before a feminine plural noun or implied noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gostei dessas ideias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't like those ideas.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "essas" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto dessas ideias, mas não concordo com todas as dessas pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like those ideas, but I don’t agree with all of those people’s ideas.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "dar"; often used in hypothetical "if" clauses (e.g., "Se eu...", "Se ele...").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I gave more time, I would help you.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esse" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu ouvi falar desse filme ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard about that movie yesterday.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esse" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gosto desse livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like that book.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (e.g., after "se" or "que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles dessem mais tempo, eu terminaria o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they gave more time, I would finish the work.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (plural masculine).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like these movies.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não gostei desses livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t like those books.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esses" (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não gosto desses filmes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like those movies.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esta" (feminine singular).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this city.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "esta" (feminine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito desta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this city.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estas" (feminine plural).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't remember the names of these people.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form used with “tu” (informal ‘you’ in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deste um presente à tua irmã?

definitions.note: Contraction of “de” + “este” (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito do sabor deste café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like the taste of this coffee.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este"; masculine singular.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this book.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este". Used with masculine singular nouns; "desta" is feminine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito do sabor deste café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like the taste of this coffee.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "este" (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto muito deste livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like this book.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estes" (masculine plural).

definitions.note: Contraction of "de" + "estes" (plural masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto destes livros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these books.

definitions.note: Often used with “a/para” to say something is intended for someone or something.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room is intended for guests.

definitions.note: past participle (feminine plural) of "destruir"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses were destroyed by the storm.

definitions.note: Past participle of "destruir"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi/está destruído").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio foi destruído pelo incêndio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was destroyed by the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos foram destruídos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were destroyed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A tempestade destrói muitas casas todos os anos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As desvantagens desse plano são claras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The disadvantages of this plan are clear.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “desviar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O carro desviou para evitar o buraco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car swerved to avoid the pothole.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for affirmative commands with você/a gente): e.g., “Desça as escadas.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, desça as escadas com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go down the stairs carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela escreveu uma explicação detalhada do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrote a detailed explanation of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She explained the problem in detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O relatório ficou bem detalhado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report turned out very detailed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse detalhe é importante.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não me lembro de todos os detalhes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t remember all the details.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands addressed to vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês detenham a violência imediatamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you stop the violence immediately.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands addressed to vocês).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que eles detenham o suspeito sem violência.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they detain the suspect without violence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia tentou deter os manifestantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tried to deter the protesters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O juiz determina a pena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge determines the sentence.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está determinada a terminar o curso este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to finish the course this year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em determinada situação, é melhor manter a calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In a certain situation, it’s better to stay calm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está determinada a terminar o curso este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to finish the course this year.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “a certain/specific” (not necessarily “determined” in the personal sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Em determinado momento, a luz acabou.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At a certain moment, the power went out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela mostrou muita determinação para terminar o curso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed a lot of determination to finish the course.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela detesta acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hates waking up early.

definitions.note: Present tense (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles detestam acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hate waking up early.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing/repeated past actions or states).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detestava acordar cedo quando era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hated waking up early when I was a child.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form meaning a completed action: “I hated / I disliked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detestei aquele filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hated that movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu detesto acordar cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate waking up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A detetive encontrou uma pista importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detective found an important clue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os detetives investigaram o caso a noite toda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detectives investigated the case all night long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O suspeito foi detido pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was detained by the police.

definitions.note: Often used as “detrás de” + noun/pronoun (“behind” something).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is behind the house.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts meaning to stop or restrain something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia tentou detê-lo antes que ele fugisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tried to stop him before he ran away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deu o livro ao amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave the book to her friend.

definitions.note: Often capitalized (Deus) when referring to the monotheistic God.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deus é amor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: God is love.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se vestiu como uma deusa na festa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dressed like a goddess at the party.

definitions.note: Plural of “deus”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os deuses da mitologia grega são famosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gods of Greek mythology are famous.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ele/ela/você). Often used after expressions of necessity, recommendation, or doubt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É importante que ele deva pedir desculpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that he should apologize.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fala devagar, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak slowly, please.

definitions.note: Used to express obligation/necessity; typically followed by an infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele deve estudar hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He must study today.

definitions.note: Used to express a logical deduction or strong probability.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela deve estar em casa agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She must be at home now.

definitions.note: From the verb “dever”; often used to express obligation (“must”) or expectation/advice (“should”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must/should study today.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vós) form; in modern Portuguese, this is mainly used in very formal/literary contexts or in Portugal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deveis estudar mais para o exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must/should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: 3rd-person plural present (they/you all) of the auxiliary verb “dever”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles devem estudar hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They must study today.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you plural) present of "dever"; can express obligation or strong recommendation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles devem estudar mais para o exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They must study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to express obligation/necessity; it can also express advice (like “should”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devemos estudar mais para o exame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: 1st-person plural present tense of "dever".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devemos estudar antes da prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should study before the test.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “dever”; commonly used to mean “owing” money or something to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou devendo cinquenta reais ao João.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I owe João fifty reais.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “dever”; used to express obligation (similar to “must/should”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou devendo estudar mais para a prova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to study more for the test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É meu dever ajudar a minha família.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is my duty to help my family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho muitos deveres para cumprir hoje.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "encontrar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "foi/estava encontrada").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A carteira foi encontrada perto do banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wallet was found near the bench.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (often used as a past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As chaves foram encontradas no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were found on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O anel foi encontrado no jardim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ring was found in the garden.

definitions.note: past participle (plural masculine) of “encontrar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos foram encontrados ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were found yesterday.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they/you all) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encontram as chaves na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They find the keys in the drawer.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially Brazilian) spoken form of “encontramos” (final -s is dropped in speech and sometimes written that way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gente se encontramo na porta do cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met at the movie theater entrance.

definitions.note: Can mean either ‘we find’ (discover/locate) or ‘we meet’ (run into/arrange to see), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós encontramos as chaves na cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found the keys in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não consigo encontrar as minhas chaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my keys.

definitions.note: Often used for meeting someone by chance; for planned meetings, Portuguese commonly uses “encontrar-se com”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrei a Ana no supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles encontraram uma solução para o problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found a solution to the problem.

definitions.native: I will find, I will meet
definitions.note: Simple future (1st person singular) of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontrarei a solução amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find the solution tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future subjunctive form, used after certain conjunctions (e.g., quando, se) to talk about a future possibility/condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eles encontrarem a chave, abrem a porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they find the key, they open the door.

definitions.native: we will find, we will meet
definitions.note: Future tense ("we" form). Can mean finding something or meeting someone, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã encontraremos um bom lugar para almoçar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will find a good place to have lunch.

definitions.native: (for us) to meet, (for us) to find
definitions.note: Personal infinitive (infinitivo pessoal), used with an explicit subject like “nós” (“we”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor encontrarmos um lugar tranquilo para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to find a quiet place to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você encontrará a chave na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the key in the drawer.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (used in hypothetical situations, often after “se” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu encontrasse as chaves, eu te avisaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found the keys, I would let you know.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraste as chaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (eu) or imperative (você) form of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eu encontre as chaves hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I find the keys today.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "encontrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrei minhas chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form (used after expressions of desire, doubt, or commands with que).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vocês encontrem a chave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontro minhas chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find my keys in my bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu encontro meus amigos no café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I meet my friends at the café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho um encontro às três da tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting at three in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used for a romantic meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai ter um encontro com o namorado hoje à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s going on a date with her boyfriend tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos encontros todas as semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have meetings every week.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "encontrar"; often used for either finding something or meeting someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela encontrou as chaves no sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found the keys on the couch.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial spelling (common in Brazil) representing the pronunciation of "encontrar" with the final -r dropped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou te encontrá amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to meet you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela me encorajou a tentar de novo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She encouraged me to try again.

definitions.note: Often used as a command (to você), especially for drivers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, encoste o carro no acostamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pull the car over onto the shoulder.

definitions.note: Can be used as a command (to você) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encoste a escada na parede com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lean the ladder against the wall carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele encostou na parede para descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaned against the wall to rest.

definitions.note: Often used with vehicles (e.g., a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O motorista encostou o carro na lateral da rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver pulled the car over to the side of the street.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe a difficult situation or someone who’s in trouble.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou encrencado porque perdi o prazo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in trouble because I missed the deadline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Precisamos encurtar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to shorten the meeting.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a street address (where someone lives or where a place is).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o seu endereço?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your address?

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form of “endireitar” (also used in some requests/suggestions with “que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu endireite a cadeira, ela para de balançar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I straighten the chair, it stops wobbling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de mais energia para terminar o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more energy to finish the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compramos enfeites para a árvore de Natal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought decorations for the Christmas tree.

definitions.note: female form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A enfermeira ajudou o paciente a se levantar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse helped the patient stand up.

definitions.note: feminine plural of “enfermeira” (female nurse)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As enfermeiras trabalham no hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses work at the hospital.

definitions.note: Male nurse; often used generically for “nurse” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O enfermeiro mediu a minha pressão arterial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse took my blood pressure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou em casa por causa de uma enfermidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed home because of an illness.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bicicleta está enferrujada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle is rusty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A bicicleta ficou enferrujada depois de ficar meses na chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle got rusty after being left in the rain for months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfim chegamos em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finally got home.

definitions.note: Often used to wrap up what you’re saying or move on to the next point in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfim, vamos começar a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anyway, let’s start the meeting.

definitions.native: stuck in, shoved in, put in
definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “enfiar”; often implies doing it quickly or forcefully.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enfiou a chave na fechadura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stuck the key in the lock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enforcou o quadro na parede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hung the picture on the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou enfurecido com a mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He became furious about the lie.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estava enganada sobre o horário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was mistaken about the time.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela se sentiu enganada pelo vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt deceived by the salesperson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está enganado sobre o horário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are mistaken about the time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi enganado pelo vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was tricked by the salesperson.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enganar"; often used with "estar" to mean someone is mistaken.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você está enganado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are mistaken.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enganar"; can describe someone who was deceived.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi enganado pelo golpista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was tricked by the scammer.

definitions.note: Masculine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estavam enganados sobre o horário da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were mistaken about the time of the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tentou me enganar, mas eu percebi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to deceive me, but I noticed.

definitions.native: to make a mistake, to be wrong
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "enganar-se" = "to be mistaken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me enganei sobre o horário da reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was mistaken about the time of the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enganei o vendedor e paguei menos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fooled the seller and paid less.

definitions.native: I made a mistake, I got it wrong
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpa, enganei-me no número.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I got the number wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpe, foi um engano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, it was a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele me enganou com aquela história.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tricked me with that story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Houve um engarrafamento enorme na estrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a huge traffic jam on the road.

definitions.note: Commonly used for choking on food/drink or gagging; can also be used figuratively (e.g., “choked up” while speaking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engasgou com um pedaço de pão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He choked on a piece of bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela estuda engenharia na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies engineering at the university.

definitions.note: female form (a woman engineer)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmã é engenheira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is an engineer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu irmão é engenheiro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an engineer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os engenheiros estão a construir uma ponte nova.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The engineers are building a new bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engoliu o comprimido com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swallowed the pill with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engoliu o comprimido com água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swallowed the pill with water.

definitions.note: Can be used for people or animals; it can also be used for things like food when it ‘fattens’ (makes you gain weight).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu engordei cinco quilos no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gained five kilos last year.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “engordar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele engordou no último ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gained weight in the last year.

definitions.note: Commonly used for becoming pregnant (often about a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela engravidou no ano passado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got pregnant last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou engraxar os sapatos antes da entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to shine my shoes before the interview.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito engraçada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very funny.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As histórias dela são engraçadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her stories are funny.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something humorous, but it can also mean something is strange depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi muito engraçado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very funny.

definitions.note: Commonly used when something seems unusual or suspicious (tone and context matter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É engraçado ele não ter respondido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s strange that he didn’t reply.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form. Can also mean “amusing” or “weird” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles são muito engraçados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very funny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A origem desse objeto é um enigma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The origin of that object is a mystery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho constante é muito enjoado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That constant noise is very annoying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do passeio de barco, eu fiquei enjoado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the boat ride, I felt nauseated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois da notícia, ele enlouqueceu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he went crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou enojado com a situação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry about the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O prédio é enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building is huge.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles têm problemas enormes para resolver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have huge problems to solve.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a simultaneous action or an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enquanto eu cozinho, ele põe a mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While I cook, he sets the table.

definitions.note: Used to express a condition (similar to “provided that”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode ficar aqui enquanto estiver tranquilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can stay here as long as you stay calm.

definitions.note: Often introduces an action happening at the same time as another.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enquanto eu cozinho, ele põe a mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While I cook, he sets the table.

definitions.note: Used to contrast two ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gosta de café, enquanto eu prefiro chá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes coffee, whereas I prefer tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gostei do enredo do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the plot of the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela enrolou o tapete e guardou no armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rolled up the rug and put it away in the closet.

definitions.note: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, "enrolar" is often used informally to mean delaying or stalling instead of doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele enrolou a entrega e só mandou o arquivo hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He delayed the delivery and only sent the file today.

definitions.native: to rehearse, to practice (for a performance)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos ensaiar a peça amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to rehearse the play tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ensaio da peça começa às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rehearsal for the play starts at seven.

definitions.note: Common in academic contexts; can also refer to a written composition or short text.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso entregar um ensaio sobre história amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to turn in an essay about history tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ensina português na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She teaches Portuguese at school.

definitions.note: past participle of “ensinar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi ensinado pelo avô a tocar violão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was taught by his grandfather to play the guitar.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "ensinar" (they teach / you all teach).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles ensinam português na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They teach Portuguese at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós ensinamos português para iniciantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We teach Portuguese to beginners.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of showing someone how to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje ensinamos como usar este aplicativo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we show how to use this app.

definitions.note: present participle / gerund of “ensinar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está ensinando português para os alunos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is teaching Portuguese to the students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gosta de ensinar português para iniciantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes to teach Portuguese to beginners.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles ensinaram português para os alunos novos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They taught Portuguese to the new students.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in hypothetical clauses (e.g., after "se" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu ensinasse português, moraria no Brasil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I taught Portuguese, I would live in Brazil.

definitions.note: Imperfect past: describes an ongoing/repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ensinava português na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She used to teach Portuguese at the school.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for affirmative formal commands: “Ensine ...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você ensine português para os alunos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you teach Portuguese to the students.

definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of “ensinar” used with “eu” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu ensinei português para um amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I taught Portuguese to a friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu ensino português para iniciantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach Portuguese to beginners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O ensino público precisa de mais investimento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Public education needs more investment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ensinou português para os alunos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She taught Portuguese to the students.

definitions.note: Colloquial spoken form (mainly in Brazil) of “ensinar” in the infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou ensiná você a cozinhar hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to teach you how to cook today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje está um dia ensolarado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is a sunny day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto de caminhar na praia ao entardecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to walk on the beach at sunset.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está entediada na aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is bored in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou entediado em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m bored at home.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estavam entediados durante a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were bored during the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme foi entediante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was boring.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, entenda que eu não posso ir hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please understand that I can't go today.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present indicative of "entender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele entende o que você está dizendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He understands what you are saying.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “entender” (they/you all understand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles entendem a explicação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They understand the explanation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós entendemos o que você quer dizer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We understand what you mean.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “entender” (used like “understanding” / “I am understanding”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m understanding better now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não consigo entender esta explicação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t understand this explanation.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "entender" for "they/you all".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles entenderam a explicação na hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They understood the explanation right away.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypotheticals, polite requests, or reported future-in-the-past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would understand better if you spoke more slowly.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) future form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele entenderá a explicação amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will understand the explanation tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used with tu (informal singular), common in European Portuguese and in some regions/registers of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entendes o que eu quero dizer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand what I mean?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (used in hypothetical situations, wishes, or after certain past expressions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se eu entendesse a pergunta, eu responderia melhor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I understood the question, I would answer better.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "entender" (he/she/you formal understood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você entendeu a pergunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you understand the question?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "entender".

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vós); mostly used in Portugal or in formal/archaic contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vós estais prontos para começar?

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form of "estar"; often used for temporary states or locations.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been sick this week.

definitions.note: Used for temporary states/conditions, locations, and many ongoing actions (with gerund).

definitions.note: Future tense (they/you plural). Often used as an auxiliary to form the future progressive (e.g., estarão estudando = will be studying).

definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form of “estar”; often used for ongoing states/background situations in the past.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present (or second-person plural in European Portuguese, formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles falam português em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They speak Portuguese at home.

definitions.note: Present tense ("we").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nós falamos português em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak Portuguese at home.
