definitions.note: Future tense (ele/ela/você). Can also be used formally as “you will like.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gostará do presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will like the gift.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gostaríamos de reservar uma mesa para duas pessoas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like to reserve a table for two people.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) form; common in Portugal and in some regions of Brazil.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu gostas de música brasileira?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like Brazilian music?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "gostar"; often used after expressions like "queria que" (I wanted that...) or in conditional/hypothetical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu queria que você gostasse deste livro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted you to like this book.

definitions.note: Informal: 2nd person singular (tu), simple past (pretérito perfeito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gostaste do filme?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you like the movie?

definitions.note: Imperfect of "gostar"; often used to express a past habit/feeling ("liked") or a polite/softened request ("would like").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gostava muito desse livro quando era criança.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really liked that book when I was a child.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all liked; used for habitual or ongoing past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eram crianças, gostavam de brincar no parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were children, they liked to play in the park.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive after expressions like “I hope,” “it’s important that,” etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que você goste do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like the movie.

definitions.note: Past (pretérito perfeito) form of "gostar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gostei muito do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the movie a lot.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (used after expressions like "Espero que...", "É importante que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que eles gostem do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they like the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gosto de aprender português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like learning Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este chá tem um gosto amargo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tea has a bitter taste.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem gosto por música clássica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a liking for classical music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Temos gostos parecidos em música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have similar tastes in music.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "gostoso"; used for food and other things that taste/feel pleasant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa sobremesa está gostosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dessert is tasty.

definitions.note: In informal speech, it can describe an attractive woman; can sound objectifying depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é muito gostosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She's really hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse bolo está gostoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cake is tasty.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person's physical attractiveness; can sound flirtatious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito gostoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very good-looking.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gostar": “(he/she/you formal) liked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gostou do filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She liked the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caiu uma gota de água na mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A drop of water fell on the table.

definitions.note: Plural of "gota".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cairam algumas gotas de chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A few drops of rain fell.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a roof/ceiling leak where water drips inside.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tem uma goteira no teto da cozinha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a leak in the kitchen ceiling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela governa o país com firmeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She governs the country firmly.

definitions.note: Used for the head of a state/province, or for the head of certain institutions (e.g., a central bank).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O governador anunciou novas medidas para a segurança pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The governor announced new measures for public safety.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O governo anunciou novas medidas econômicas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government announced new economic measures.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) form of "governar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela governou o país por quatro anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She governed the country for four years.

definitions.note: Often refers to metal bars on windows/doors (like security bars). Not related to English "grades" (school marks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As grades da janela estão enferrujadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The window bars are rusty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As coisas melhoraram gradualmente ao longo do ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Things improved gradually over the year.

definitions.note: Often refers to receiving an academic degree or the degree itself (especially in higher education).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai terminar a graduação em engenharia este ano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to finish her engineering degree this year.

definitions.note: Feminine when it means “grass” (a grama).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A grama do jardim está bem verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grass in the garden is very green.

definitions.note: Masculine when it means the unit of weight (o grama); very common in the plural (gramas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso de duzentas gramas de queijo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two hundred grams of cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As crianças brincam no gramado do parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children play on the park lawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me emprestar o grampeador?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me the stapler?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou a estudar gramática portuguesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m studying Portuguese grammar.

definitions.note: Informal (Brazilian Portuguese).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou sem grana este mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m out of money this month.

definitions.note: Often means “big/large” (usually after the noun). Before a noun, it can mean “great” in the sense of important/admired (e.g., “um grande amigo” = “a great friend”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A casa é grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is big.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As casas são grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses are big.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sou muito grata pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sinto muita gratidão por tudo o que você fez por mim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of gratitude for everything you did for me.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to say who/what you’re grateful for (e.g., "grato a você").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sou muito grato pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Somos muito gratos pela sua ajuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada do museu é gratuita, então você pode entrar gratuitamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum entry is free, so you can go in for free.

definitions.note: Often used for services, events, or items that cost no money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada é gratuita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free.

definitions.note: Commonly used for temperature (graus Celsius/Fahrenheit) and for levels or intensity (e.g., a high degree of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje está a 30 graus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s 30 degrees.

definitions.note: Often used for levels in school or hierarchy (e.g., primeiro grau).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está no primeiro grau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in first grade.

definitions.note: Plural of "grau". Commonly used for temperature (°C/°F) and angles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoje faz 30 graus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s 30 degrees.

definitions.note: Often refers to an audio/voice recorder or recording device.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um gravador para gravar as aulas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a recorder to record the classes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele colocou uma gravata azul para a reunião.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put on a blue tie for the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele tem várias gravatas no armário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has several ties in the closet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O acidente foi grave, mas ninguém morreu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident was serious, but nobody died.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele ficou gravemente ferido no acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was seriously injured in the accident.

definitions.note: Adjective in the plural form (masculine or feminine, depending on the noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: São problemas graves, mas vamos resolvê-los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are serious problems, but we’re going to solve them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A gravidade mantém a Terra em órbita ao redor do Sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gravity keeps the Earth in orbit around the Sun.

definitions.note: Often used for the seriousness of a situation, problem, or offense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele não entendeu a gravidade do problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t understand the seriousness of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está no terceiro mês de gravidez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is in the third month of pregnancy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela gravou a aula no celular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She recorded the class on her phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O joalheiro gravou o nome dela no anel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jeweler engraved her name on the ring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele respondeu com graça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replied with grace.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression "fazer graça" (to joke around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele fez uma graça para nos fazer rir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a joke to make us laugh.

definitions.note: Common in religious contexts (e.g., "pela graça de Deus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi pela graça de Deus que tudo deu certo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was by God's grace that everything worked out.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “graças a …” meaning “thanks to …” (e.g., “Graças a Deus” = “Thank God”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Graças a você, conseguimos terminar o trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks to you, we managed to finish the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela dançava com graças.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She danced with grace.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é grega e mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Greek and lives in Lisbon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está estudando literatura grega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is studying Greek literature.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a Greek person; it can also refer to the Greek language depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é grego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Greek.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu estudo grego na universidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Greek at the university.

definitions.note: plural masculine (refers to more than one male person or a mixed group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os turistas gregos chegaram ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greek tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural of "grego" (a Greek person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os gregos têm uma história muito antiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greeks have a very ancient history.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “(he/she/it) grilled.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele grelhou o frango no carvão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grilled the chicken over charcoal.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a work stoppage/protest by workers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os professores fizeram greve por melhores salários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers went on strike for better pay.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the verb "estar" (e.g., "estou gripado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou gripado e vou ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I'm going to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou com gripe e vou ficar em casa hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I’m going to stay home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu avô está com o cabelo bem grisalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather’s hair is very gray.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “gritar” (also used in commands like “Shout!” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela grita quando está com medo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shouts when she’s scared.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “gritar” (used like “shouting/yelling” or “while shouting/yelling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele entrou na sala gritando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walked into the room shouting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Não precisa gritar comigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don't need to shout at me.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) for “they” (and also “you all” in Brazil).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles gritaram quando viram o acidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They shouted when they saw the accident.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gritar" for the first person singular (eu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu gritei porque estava com medo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted because I was scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ouvi um grito na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a shout in the street.

definitions.note: Plural of “grito”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ouvimos gritos na rua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard shouts in the street.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "gritar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele gritou com o irmão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted at his brother.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone feeling unwell, dizzy, or slow (for example, from lack of sleep, alcohol, or medication).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Depois do remédio, fiquei grogue o resto do dia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the medicine, I felt groggy for the rest of the day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "grosso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A corda é muito grossa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rope is very thick.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As piadas dele eram grosseiras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His jokes were rude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi grosseiro com a garçonete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was rude to the waitress.

definitions.note: Often refers to physical size or thickness; for people it can mean “fat” (can sound rude depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele comprou um livro grosso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought a thick book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O nosso grupo vai se encontrar às sete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our group is going to meet at seven.

definitions.note: Plural of "grupo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os grupos de estudantes apresentaram seus projetos hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The groups of students presented their projects today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este gráfico mostra as vendas do último mês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chart shows last month's sales.

definitions.note: Often used after the noun: "entrada grátis" = "free entry".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A entrada é grátis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry is free.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with women).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está grávida de três meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is three months pregnant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pão tem grãos de trigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bread has wheat grains.

definitions.note: Plural of "grão"; often used for cereal grains or coffee beans depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei grãos de café para fazer um café mais fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought coffee beans to make fresher coffee.

definitions.note: Often used for a person whose job is to protect or watch over a place (e.g., a security guard). It can be used with either article: o guarda / a guarda.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guarda está na entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guard is at the entrance of the building.

definitions.note: From the verb "guardar"; often used for keeping/storing something in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guarda as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps the keys in her bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você pode me passar um guardanapo, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me a napkin, please?

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while keeping/storing" or "(is) keeping/storing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou guardando os documentos na gaveta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m keeping the documents in the drawer.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "guardar" (often used to mean "while watching over" or "(is) looking after").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela está guardando as crianças enquanto eu trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s looking after the kids while I work.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something away in a safe place or saving it for later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou guardar estas fotos numa caixa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to keep these photos in a box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O cão vai guardar a casa à noite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog will guard the house at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os guardas vigiam a entrada do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guards watch the entrance to the building.

definitions.note: Usually a formal command (“you” singular) or the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “é importante que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarde este recibo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep this receipt.

definitions.native: I kept, I saved, I put away
definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardei o dinheiro na carteira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the money away in my wallet.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guardou as chaves na bolsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept the keys in her purse.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guardar” (ele/ela/você).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele guardou os brinquedos depois de brincar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put away the toys after playing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ontem à noite, vimos um guaxinim perto do lixo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night, we saw a raccoon near the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guerra acabou depois de muitos anos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war ended after many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As guerras mudaram a história do país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wars changed the country’s history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guerreiro voltou para casa depois da batalha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warrior returned home after the battle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guia explicou a história da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide explained the history of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprei um guia de viagem para o Porto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a travel guidebook for Porto.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O guindaste levantou a viga de aço com cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crane lifted the steel beam carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “guiar” for ele/ela/você.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela guiou o grupo até a entrada do museu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guided the group to the museum entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu toco guitarra todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play guitar every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A guitarrista toca muito bem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitarist plays very well.

definitions.note: Usually masculine: o gás.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gás acabou e precisamos comprar outro botijão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas ran out and we need to buy another gas cylinder.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem uma irmã gêmea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a twin sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmão é gêmeo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a twin.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os gêmeos têm o mesmo aniversário.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twins have the same birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na ficha, você precisa indicar seu gênero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, you need to indicate your gender.

definitions.note: Common for categories like music, movies, and books.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qual é o gênero desse filme?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What genre is this movie?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é um gênio em matemática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a genius at math.

definitions.note: Used for a magical being (like in stories); in Portuguese, this sense is less common than “gênio” = “genius”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No filme, o gênio sai da lâmpada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, the genie comes out of the lamp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A escola reuniu gênios da matemática para dar uma palestra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school brought together geniuses in mathematics to give a talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muita habilidade para resolver problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of skill in solving problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muitas habilidades em programação.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has many programming skills.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é um cozinheiro muito habilidoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a very skillful cook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os habitantes desta cidade são muito simpáticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inhabitants of this city are very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É habitual ele chegar cedo ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s usual for him to arrive early to work.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the subjunctive (often after que, like in “Espero que haja…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que haja tempo para conversar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope there is time to talk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu quero um hambúrguer com queijo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a hamburger with cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem muitos interesses, como música e esportes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has many interests, like music and sports.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of “interessar”. Often used in the pattern “interesso-me por/em …” or “interesso por/em …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu me interesso por música brasileira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m interested in Brazilian music.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito perfeito) of "interessar" in the sense of "to interest".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O filme me interessou bastante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie interested me a lot.

definitions.note: This is the infinitive form of "interessar" with the final -r dropped and an accent added, typically used before an attached object pronoun (e.g., "interessá-lo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quero interessá-lo pelo assunto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to interest him in the subject.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu não quero interferir na sua decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to interfere in your decision.

definitions.native: to interrupt, to get involved (in something)
definitions.note: Often used with "em": "interferir em" = to interfere in/with something (often in a negative or unwanted way).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He keeps getting involved in everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A sala interior é mais silenciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inner room is quieter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O interior da casa é bem iluminado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inside of the house is very well lit.

definitions.note: In Portuguese, this often refers to areas away from the coast and big cities (the “interior” of a state/region).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles se mudaram para o interior para ter uma vida mais tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They moved to the countryside to have a quieter life.

definitions.note: In linguistics, it refers to a learner’s developing language system while learning a second language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A interlíngua de um estudante muda com o tempo, à medida que ele aprende português.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A student's interlanguage changes over time as they learn Portuguese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A reunião foi interminável.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was endless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este é um projeto internacional.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an international project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A internet está lenta hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The internet is slow today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A investigação interna terminou ontem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The internal investigation ended yesterday.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os documentos internos não podem sair do escritório.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The internal documents can’t leave the office.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "interpretar". It can mean understood/explained or translated (e.g., in interpreting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mensagem foi interpretada como uma ameaça.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The message was interpreted as a threat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É difícil interpretar o que ele quis dizer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to interpret what he meant.

definitions.note: Used for performing a character in theater/film/TV.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela vai interpretar a protagonista no filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s going to play the main character in the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A interpretação do texto é muito importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The interpretation of the text is very important.

definitions.note: Often used for an actor’s or performer’s work in a movie, play, or show.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A interpretação dela no filme foi excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her performance in the movie was excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele foi interrogado pela polícia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was interrogated by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A interrogação do professor deixou a turma em silêncio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher’s question left the class silent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esqueci de colocar a interrogação no final da frase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to put the question mark at the end of the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desculpe interromper, mas tenho uma pergunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry to interrupt, but I have a question.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of “interromper” (he/she/it interrupted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele interrompeu a reunião para atender o telefone.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He interrupted the meeting to answer the phone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of “interromper”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A reunião foi interrompida por causa do alarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was interrupted because of the alarm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O serviço foi interrompido por causa da chuva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The service was interrupted because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O interruptor está ao lado da porta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light switch is next to the door.

definitions.note: Often used for a short break between classes, meetings, or parts of an event (e.g., school recess).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos fazer um intervalo de dez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take a ten-minute break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia interveio para acabar com a briga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police intervened to put an end to the fight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A intervenção do professor ajudou a resolver o conflito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher’s intervention helped resolve the conflict.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é muito intolerante com opiniões diferentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very intolerant of different opinions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A intolerância pode causar conflitos desnecessários.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Intolerance can cause unnecessary conflicts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fiquei intrigado com o que ele disse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was intrigued by what he said.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é mais introvertido do que o irmão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more introverted than his brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O segurança tirou o intruso do prédio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The security guard removed the intruder from the building.

definitions.note: Can refer to someone who translates spoken language or to a performer who interprets music/acting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela trabalha como intérprete em conferências internacionais.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works as an interpreter at international conferences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A inundação deixou muitas ruas debaixo d’água.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flood left many streets underwater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: As inundações destruíram várias casas na cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floods destroyed several houses in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O exército decidiu invadir o país vizinho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army decided to invade the neighboring country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O exército invadiu a cidade ao amanhecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army invaded the city at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele sentiu inveja do sucesso dela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt envy of her success.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense ("I envy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu invejo a sua coragem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy your courage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este time parece invencível nesta temporada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team seems invincible this season.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa história foi inventada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That story was made up.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to make something up” (a story, excuse, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele inventou uma desculpa para faltar ao trabalho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made up an excuse to miss work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O inventor criou um novo tipo de bateria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inventor created a new type of battery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela inventou uma desculpa para faltar à aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She made up an excuse to miss class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essa invenção mudou a forma como as pessoas se comunicam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That invention changed the way people communicate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No inverno, faz frio aqui.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the winter, it’s cold here.

definitions.note: Plural form of "investigador".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os investigadores chegaram cedo para analisar as provas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigators arrived early to analyze the evidence.

definitions.note: Gerund (ongoing action), often used with “estar” to mean “to be investigating.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia está investigando o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia vai investigar o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to investigate the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia abriu uma investigação sobre o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police opened an investigation into the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A polícia investigou o caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police investigated the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este investimento vai trazer bons resultados no futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This investment will bring good results in the future.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela quer investir em ações.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to invest in stocks.

definitions.note: Common in European Portuguese; in Brazilian Portuguese, "vestir" is more common for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vou investir o casaco porque está frio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to put on my coat because it's cold.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: À noite, as estrelas ficam quase invisíveis por causa das luzes da cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, the stars become almost invisible because of the city lights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O gás é invisível, mas é perigoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas is invisible, but it’s dangerous.

definitions.note: Almost always used in the expression “ao invés de …” (also commonly “em vez de …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ao invés de estudar, ele ficou vendo TV.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of studying, he kept watching TV.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No início do filme, ele está em casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the beginning of the movie, he is at home.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form, used before a feminine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela tem inúmeras ideias para o projeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has countless ideas for the project.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Essas ferramentas são inúteis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those tools are useless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este computador velho é inútil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This old computer is useless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu como iogurte no café da manhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat yogurt for breakfast.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary to form the near future: ir + infinitive (e.g., vou + infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu vou ir visitar meus avós amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to visit my grandparents tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” + place (e.g., ir ao mercado = go to the market).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preciso ir agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A ira dele foi diminuindo com o tempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger gradually decreased over time.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular (eu) simple future of ir.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã irei ao médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go to the doctor.

definitions.note: First-person singular (eu) future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã irei ao mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go to the market.

definitions.note: Future subjunctive of "ir" (used after certain conjunctions like "quando", "se", "antes que").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quando eles irem ao mercado, vão comprar frutas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they go to the market, they’re going to buy fruit.

definitions.note: 1st person plural ("we") in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã iremos ao mercado cedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will go to the market early.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") in the future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã iremos ao cinema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will go to the movies.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the verb/auxiliary “ir” (often used to talk about something that would happen, or a future-in-the-past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu iria com você, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go with you, but I’m sick.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "ir" (to go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu iria com você, mas estou doente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go with you, but I'm sick.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary with an infinitive (e.g., "iriam fazer" = "would do / were going to do").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles iriam comprar um carro, mas desistiram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were going to buy a car, but they changed their minds.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for women or feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha professora é irlandesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Irish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele é irlandês.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Irish.

definitions.note: Personal infinitive of "ir" used with "nós" (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: É melhor irmos agora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmã mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Can mean a biological brother or be used informally to refer to a close male friend (like “bro”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmão mora em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother lives in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Plural of “irmão”. Can also refer to siblings (brothers and sisters) in some contexts, but “irmãos” literally means “brothers”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenho dois irmãos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two brothers.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “irmão”; can express small size or affection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O meu irmãozinho ainda está na escola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My little brother is still at school.

definitions.note: plural feminine form of “irmã”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Minhas irmãs moram em Lisboa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters live in Lisbon.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "irmã"; often expresses affection (like “sis” or “little sis”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A minha irmãzinha adora desenhar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My little sister loves to draw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O horário do ônibus é irregular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus schedule is irregular.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse detalhe é irrelevante para a nossa decisão.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That detail is irrelevant to our decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse bolo é irresistível.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cake is irresistible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Foi irresponsável da sua parte dirigir depois de beber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was irresponsible of you to drive after drinking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho me irrita muito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise irritates me a lot.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela ficou irritada com o atraso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got irritated about the delay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele está irritado com o trânsito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is irritated about the traffic.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles estão irritados com o barulho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are irritated by the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esses comentários irritam muita gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments irritate (annoy) a lot of people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esse barulho é muito irritante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is very annoying.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito perfeito) of "irritar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O barulho do trânsito irritou o vizinho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic noise irritated the neighbor.

definitions.note: Future tense form of "ir". As an auxiliary, it introduces an infinitive (e.g., "irá fazer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ele irá estudar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will study tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (ele/ela/você) simple future of “ir” (to go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela irá ao médico amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will go to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tu) future tense; often sounds formal in Brazil (where “você vai” is more common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amanhã, irás ao médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, you will go to the doctor.

definitions.note: 3rd person plural (they) of the verb/auxiliary “ir” in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles irão viajar amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will travel tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (eles/elas/vocês) future tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eles irão ao mercado amanhã.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will go to the market tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "ir"; often used to talk about what someone would do in a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se tivéssemos tempo, iríamos ao cinema hoje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had time, we would go to the movies today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O pescador colocou a isca no anzol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman put the bait on the hook.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Islamism is a topic debated in many countries.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Icelandic and lives in Lisbon.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Icelandic.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Islam is practiced in many countries.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in an isolated place.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something or someone is apart from others (not connected or included).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an isolated case.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Styrofoam cooler keeps the drinks cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Você tem um isqueiro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a lighter?

definitions.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun used to refer to a thing/idea (not usually a person), often something already mentioned or near the listener.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is very important.

definitions.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun (used for things/ideas, not people), often for something close to the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Isto é muito importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is very important.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to refer to a woman)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ela é italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is Italian.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks Italian very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estou a aprender italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Italian.

definitions.note: plural masculine form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Italian tourists arrived yesterday.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Há muitos italianos nesta cidade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Italians in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The list has three items.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meu aniversário é em janeiro.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows are open.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dinner is ready.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She eats dinner at eight o'clock at night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you take the umbrella.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a mild fever.

definitions.note: Often used to describe doing something gently or without much intensity (not the adjective “light”).

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.note: Present tense (eu) form of "levar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eu levo meu filho à escola todos os dias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take my son to school every day.

definitions.note: Indirect object pronoun. It can also mean “to you” in formal address (e.g., to você/o senhor/a senhora).

definitions.note: Indirect object pronoun (plural); used with verbs that take an indirect object (often translated with “to/for”).

definitions.note: past participle of "ler"; used with auxiliary verbs (e.g., "ter", "haver") or as an adjective

definitions.note: Past participle of "ler"; used with "ter/haver" or in the passive (plural masculine).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you later.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called me last night.
